# dsh-helux-tunnel

A [DSH] (DSH) plugin that turns a **pre-created, named Cloudflare
Tunnel** on and off from a **Helux

Tunnel** panel in the left sidebar. When ON,
the tunnel publishes the local DSH Web UI on **your ow

n hostname**. When OFF,
DSH stays local at **http://127.0.0.1:3080**.

Version 2 adds a second button, **Copy launch URL**, which copies DSH's one-time
launch URL (`https:

//<your-host>/?token=...`) from the token DSH keeps only in
memory, so the first public visit works

without hunting through the terminal.
Version 2.1 adds **Pair device (QR)**, which shows that same l

aunch URL as a QR
code for the Helux Android app. Version 2.2 makes the hostname configurable and
ru
ns on Windows as well as Linux and macOS.

The plugin is built for DSH `0.2.1-rc.5` and `0.2.2-rc.1` (Cordis plugin model,
Host services in Nod
e, Client module in the Web page).
## Use your own domain

Nothing in this plugin is tied to the author's domain. Each deployment runs its
own `cloudflared` wi

th its own tunnel and credentials, so no traffic ever passes
through anyone else's server.

With **no plugin configuration**, the plugin adopts whatever hostname your
tunnel's `config.yml` alr

tunnel's `config.yml` already publishes:

| `cloudflaredPath` | *(PATH)* |

Absolute path to the binary. |
| `cloudflaredHome` | `~/.cloudflared` | Directory with `config.yml`

and credentials. |
| `accessCheck` | `true` | Probe the public hostname for Cloudflare Access. |

Full guide: **docs/CONFIGURATION.md**.
Windows: **docs/WINDOWS.md**.
## Platform support
| Platform | Status |

| Linux | Supported |
| macOS | Supported |
| Windows 10/11 | Supported - see docs/WINDOWS.md |

The Host half is plain Node.js with no native modules. Windows differences that
are handled for you:

`taskkill /T` instead of `SIGTERM` (Windows has no
signals, and `/T` is what stops a wrapper's gran

dchild), `.exe`/`.com`-only
binary resolution (a `.cmd` cannot be spawned without a shell), quoted `

PATH`
entries, and `%USERPROFILE%` path display. Those rules live in
`src/host/platform.ts` and are
tested on every platform, not just Windows.
## What the plugin does and does not touch
| Item | Value |

| Public hostname | Yours - from plugin config, else from `config.yml` |
| Local service | `http://1

27.0.0.1:3080` by default, loopback only |
| Tunnel type | Named tunnel, already created by you |
|

Credentials | `<cloudflared-home>/<tunnel-id>.json` |
| Tunnel config | `<cloudflared-home>/config.y

ml` |
| Process | `cloudflared tunnel --config <config.yml> --no-autoupdate run <tunnel-id>` |

The plugin **never** creates a tunnel, **never** uses a quick tunnel
(`trycloudflare.com`), **never*

* generates a random URL, and **never** edits
`config.yml`, credentials, DNS, or Cloudflare Access p

rates a random URL, and **never** edits
`config.yml`, credentials, DNS, or Cloudflare Access policy.
## Default OFF — the core guarantee

- The tunnel is OFF at plugin load and at every DSH start/restart.
- Nothing auto-starts on DSH boot

, plugin activation, browser reload, or HMR.
- The only ways to start it are the sidebar switch and

the `tunnel_start` agent
tool (which the agent may call only when you explicitly ask in chat).
- Pre

ssing OFF terminates the `cloudflared` child: `SIGTERM` then `SIGKILL` on
Linux and macOS, `taskkill

/T` then `/T /F` on Windows, which also stops any
wrapper's grandchild. The stop is recorded either

way.
- Unloading the plugin or shutting DSH down kills the child process.
- State is persisted unde

r `~/.dsh/data/helux-tunnel/state.json`, but every load
forces it back to `enabled: false`; a previo

us ON is never resumed.
- The DSH launch token is never persisted. It exists only in DSH process mem

r resumed.
- The DSH launch token is never persisted. It exists only in DSH process memory,
[该节后续省略]
## Requirements

1. DSH Web profile (`dsh --profile web ...`) on `127.0.0.1:3080`.
2. The `cloudflared` binary on `PA

TH`, or `cloudflaredPath` in the plugin config.
3. An existing named tunnel with `config.yml` and `<

tunnel-id>.json` in
`~/.cloudflared` (or `cloudflaredHome`).
4. The tunnel config must route **your*
* hostname to the local DSH Web UI.

The plugin checks all five prerequisites before every start and shows every
missing one in the panel

. It installs nothing. The fifth, **DSH host trust**,
asks this DSH instance whether it accepts your

public hostname on `/api`; see
Configuration for why that matters.
## Security behavior

- When ON, `https://<host>` is **public unless Cloudflare Access is
enabled**. The panel states that

and adds **“Warning: public without Access
policy”** when its public-URL probe sees an unprotected

response.
- The plugin never disables, bypasses, or weakens Cloudflare Access. If Access
redirects t

he probe to `*.cloudflareaccess.com` (or answers 401/403), the panel
reports that Access appears to

be protecting the hostname.
- Credentials, tunnel secrets, API tokens, and the DSH launch token are

never
displayed in the UI, the tools, or the log. Log lines are redacted: long
secret/UUID-shaped to

kens and `token=`/`secret:`-style values become
`[redacted]`.
- The launch URL is masked everywhere

except the clipboard: the UI shows only
`?token=••••abcd` (last four characters). The full value is

returned once by
the local-only `POST /api/helux-tunnel/launch-url`, copied, and discarded. It
is ne

ver persisted, and a copy toast warns that it is like a password.
- Control endpoints (`/api/helux-t

unnel/start`, `/stop`, `/access-check`,
`/launch-url`) accept only loopback requests (`Host: 127.0.0

.1`, `localhost`,
`::1`, etc.) and reject any request carrying Cloudflare/proxy forwarding
headers.

Read-only status is available through the tunnel; mutations and the
launch token are not.
- Starting
/stopping does not create or modify any Cloudflare resource.
